ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Hint: Please answer the question requiring a floating-point number with one decimal place and provide the final value, e.g., 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, at the end. 
Question: Determine the DC voltage at point "B" in the circuit, ignoring any "loading" effects of the transistor’s base current on the voltage divider, as shown in the figure. The DC voltage at point "B" is ______VDC.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Determine the DC voltage at point "B" in the circuit, ignoring any "loading" effects of the transistor’s base current on the voltage divider, as shown in the figure. The DC voltage at point "B" is ______ VDC.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, point B is the middle node of the bias voltage-divider network; above it, it is connected through an 81 kΩ resistor to the power rail labeled VCC = +12 VDC, and below it, it is connected through a 10 kΩ resistor to ground. To the left, point B is connected through a 47 µF capacitor to input node A, and to the right, it is connected through a 33 kΩ resistor to the transistor base. Reasoning: When performing DC analysis, the 47 µF coupling capacitor is regarded as an open circuit, so the left-side input network does not affect point B. The problem asks to ignore the loading effect of the transistor base current on the voltage divider, so the branch through 33 kΩ to the base also does not change the divided voltage value. Therefore, the voltage at point B is determined by the unloaded voltage divider composed of 81 kΩ and 10 kΩ: V_B = 12 V × 10 kΩ / (81 kΩ + 10 kΩ) = 12 × 10 / 91 = 1.3187 V, approximately 1.3 VDC.
